summary:
Récolte+ is a web platform that helps smallholder farmers in Togo make better decisions using open NASA data. It answers three questions in plain language: should I irrigate tomorrow, will heat threaten my crop, and what should I plant over the next three years?
Farmers face irregular rain, rising heat and soils exhausted by repeated crops, yet lack simple tools linked to satellite data. Récolte+ loads NASA POWER data live (14-day series and 20 years of rainfall history) and shows SMAP and GPM as satellite sources, with simulated values for now. Explainable rules, not a black box, turn this data into advice. The platform compares nine crops, builds three 3-year rotation plans and scores each on soil health, water saving, income and drought resilience. Every recommendation cites the data behind it.
This matters because better irrigation and rotation choices save water, protect soil and reduce harvest losses, while putting NASA data within reach of farmers who need it most. Our prototype is demonstrated for Kara, Togo, and can scale across West Africa.
details:
How it works
Récolte+ is a web platform that runs in any browser, on a phone or a computer. A farmer opens a dashboard for a plot in Kara, Togo, and gets three kinds of help:
Irrigation advice. The platform reads soil moisture and forecast rain. A simple rule decides: for example, rice needs no extra water above 70 % soil moisture.
Heat alert. A warning appears before the stress threshold, around 35 °C for rice at flowering.
Rotation planner. The farmer enters soil condition, how many seasons the same crop was grown, possible crops and priorities (soil, water, income, drought). Récolte+ compares nine crops, builds three 3-year plans and scores each on soil health, water saving, relative income and resilience. Scores use the nitrogen left by legumes, crop variety and the 20-year rainfall trend from NASA POWER, loaded on demand.
Advice is written in short sentences with a colour and a clear word, can be read aloud, and cites the data behind it. A chart compares the plot sensor with the satellite and explains the gap.
Benefits
Water is used only when needed.
Heat stress is flagged early.
Rotation choices protect the soil.
Advice is simple, transparent and needs no expensive equipment: satellite data alone is enough.
Expected impact
Less wasted water, fewer harvest losses and healthier soils for smallholder farmers, who are the most exposed to climate change. NASA POWER covers the whole planet, so new regions and crops need only new rules and languages. Next steps: connect real SMAP and GPM data, add vegetation data (MODIS, Landsat, ECOSTRESS), pilot real sensors in Kara and validate the scores with agronomists.
Tools and technologies (adaptez à votre vrai développement)
Front end: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages with Git/GitHub.
Data: NASA POWER REST API (daily and monthly); SMAP and GPM displayed as sources with simulated values.
Hardware: soil-moisture and temperature sensor (demo values in the prototype; real sensors planned for the Kara pilot).
AI: an AI assistant (Claude) helped us structure and draft the project; the recommendation rules are fixed, transparent rules.
What makes it creative
It shows the plot sensor and the satellite side by side and explains why they differ.
It speaks plain language with colours and read-aloud advice, for farmers with limited digital literacy.
Explainable rules replace a black box, and every recommendation names its data.
The rotation planner adapts to the farmer's priorities and to 20 years of local rainfall.
Real and demo data are clearly labelled.
Factors we considered
Farmers' reality: smallholders, limited connectivity, little spare income, a simple light page.
Scientific validity: thresholds from crop knowledge, scores presented as indicative, validation planned with agronomists.
Data scale: the satellite sees a grid cell of several kilometres, the sensor sees one plot.
Honesty: SMAP, GPM and sensor values are simulated for now and marked as such.
Local context: local soil types, crop traits, and relative income instead of prices, which change by market.
Responsibility: advice supports decisions, it does not guarantee yields.
